probing_questions: Which sections, in what order, with what budget, and what must each make the reader grasp?
Which exhibit, of which registry kind, in which section, drawn from which rows, to make the reader grasp what?
What in the memo does the page not carry, and why?

problematique: A memo and its findings are to become a page a reader grasps on the first pass and keeps a model of. Plan the page: the sections in order with a word budget and the one thing each must make the reader grasp; the exhibits — from the registry's kinds only — each tied to a section and to the rows it draws on, with its didactic aim; and what the memo says that the page will not carry, and why. Optimise one thing: time to clarity at depth. Balance text, tables, drawn exhibits, images and sidebars; a page is not the memo with pictures, it is the memo re-cut for the eye.
researcher_question: What page, in which sections and with which exhibits, lets this reader grasp the memo on the first pass?
